To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pigeons' initial link responding under concurrent-chain schedules with nondifferential, terminal links is influenced by the primary reinforcement delivered in those links, but not by the differential stimuli in terminal links.
the initial-link stimuli that were correlated with the larger food amount were chosen more frequently than the other initial-link stimulus in 57 of 61 cases.

the effects of primary reinforcement are observed in the initial-link stimuli when the terminal-link stimuli are nondifferentia; that the effects of the amount of primary reinforcement are greater than those of the durations of the schedules of primary reinforcement; and that the effects of these manipulations on the choice of initial-link stimuli are greater than those on the choice of terminal-link stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of primary reinforcement on behavior in concurrent-chains schedule.
the effects of primary reinforcement on behavior in a concurrent-chains schedule with nondifferential terminal-link stimuli.
the effect of the primary reinforcement on initial- and terminal- link responding.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of the terminal-link stimuli on initial-link responding depends on the nature of the terminal-link schedule.
primary reinforment is the most important factor in determining initial-link responding.
the effects of primary reinforcement on choice behavior are more complex and less easily explained than previously thought.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initial-link stimuli are conditioned reinforcers and that the terminal-link stimuli are conditioned punishers.
differential initial-link responding is not necessarily a function of conditioned reinforcement, but rather is a function of the correlation between stimuli and primary reinforcers.

primary reinforcement is the major factor determining initial-link responding, while secondary reinforcement (conditioned reinforcement) is the major factor affecting choice between terminal-link alternatives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
primary reinforcement can have a direct effect on responding in initial links, even when terminal-link stimuli are nondifferential.
pigeons' initial link responding is sensitive to the differential value of the terminal link.
pigeons' choice behavior in concurrent-chains procedures is not necessarily determined solely by the terminal link.
